description: An assistant principal must approve a student's re-entry plan after a short suspension, including the student's return schedule, transition support, counseling check-ins, restorative meeting arrangements, and family-schedule coordination, with input from the student's teacher and school counselor.

shared_context.S1: An eighth-grade student is scheduled to return next Monday after a three-day suspension for a hallway altercation.
shared_context.S2: Ms. Grant approves the student's binding re-entry and behavior-support plan.
shared_context.S3: The current draft returns the student to the regular schedule, includes a weekly counselor check-in, and schedules a restorative conference after school during the first week back.
shared_context.S4: The school normally reviews a re-entry plan with the student's teacher and counselor before it is finalized.
shared_context.S5: Once the teacher and counselor have each reported their relevant observations, Ms. Grant completes the routine review and may finalize the plan without waiting for additional schedule proposals.

PF1.text: Mr. Bell observed that the student's altercations consistently occur during crowded passing periods. Because this trigger is structural to the regular passing-period schedule, the student's return schedule itself must change from a regular return to a staggered return for the full first 10 school days, rather than relying only on a hallway-route adjustment. Mr. Bell also documented that the peer assigned as the draft's mentor has a conflict with the student; because of that conflict, the peer-mentor assignment must be removed from the plan entirely and must not be reassigned to another student. He recorded these observations in his classroom notebook this week, but they have not yet been entered into the behavior-support system.

PF2.text: Ms. Ortiz reviewed the student's counseling file and confirmed with the guardian yesterday that the student must provide evening care for a younger sibling, so an after-school restorative conference is impossible and the meeting must occur during the school day. Because the student must provide evening care, the plan must include a family-schedule-coordination commitment to ensure school-day commitments do not conflict with the caregiving responsibility. Recent counseling notes also show escalating anxiety around returning to school, so the student needs daily counselor check-ins for exactly the first 10 school days rather than the weekly check-in in the draft. These updates have not yet been entered into the re-entry draft.

acceptance_conditions: The student must begin with a staggered return schedule.
The student must receive adult-escorted transition support for exactly 10 school days.
The peer mentor arrangement must be removed entirely rather than reassigned.
The student must receive daily counselor check-ins for exactly 10 school days.
The restorative meeting must occur during the school day.
A formal re-entry behavior-plan documentation commitment must be recorded.
A family-schedule coordination commitment must be recorded.
The settlement must explicitly mark that the restorative meeting is during the school day and that family-schedule coordination is required.

content_checks.C7: any('documentation' in c['type'] and 'behavior' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('family' in c['detail'] and 'coordination' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The teacher's observation requires changing the return_schedule to a staggered return, setting transition_support_days to exactly 10, setting peer_mentor_assignment to removed or none, and documenting the observation in a behavior-related commitment.

The counselor's file review changes check-ins to daily for exactly 10 school days, requires the restorative meeting during the school day, and requires both a family-and-coordination commitment and an explicit family_schedule_coordination_required decision.
